title: aid-test-resource-map-v1
description: A source-derived map of the resources one run unit touches, and the namespace each lives in. Every entry cites the file and line that justifies it, because the whole point of this artifact is to replace a grep's opinion with a reader's ability to check. Nothing here executes a test.

source_paths.description: The unit's own sources, plus every file reached by following `source`/`.` directives within the depth cap.

follow_depth_cap.description: Recorded, not implied: a reader must be able to tell whether a helper three levels down was actually read or merely out of reach.

unresolved_sources.description: A `source`/`load` directive whose target could not be read — computed at runtime, missing, or beyond the depth cap. Each caps this unit's classifications at `unknown`: a unit with unreadable dependencies cannot be proven isolated.

reason.description: Why it could not be read. A helper that EXISTS but sits beyond the depth cap is a different fact from one that is missing, and both differ from a path assembled at runtime — the remedy differs in each case.

capped_at_unknown.description: True when unresolved_sources is non-empty. Every namespace in `resources` is then `unknown` regardless of what the readable portion suggested.

location.description: file:line, relative to the project root. The justification, not a hint.

detail.description: What was actually seen — the path, the port, the helper name. Free text, but never empty: an entry nobody can identify is not evidence.

via.description: Present when the classification comes from a helper the unit sources rather than from its own body. Names the helper, so a per-test guarantee is attributable rather than assumed.

allOf.$comment: A `shared` classification is the one that keeps a unit out of every pool, so it must be the best-evidenced entry in the map, never the residue of a pattern match. The schema cannot check that a location is CORRECT, but it can refuse an entry that names none.
